title: TD(0), SARSA, and Q-learning on the cliff
brief: Estimate values from single steps, show that batch TD finds the maximum-likelihood model's values, then learn to control the cliff walk two ways and see them choose different paths.
hints: The TD error is r + gamma * V[s2] * (not terminated) - V[s]. Forgetting the terminal mask bootstraps from a state that has no future.
In certainty_equivalence, solve only on the states that were ever left: np.linalg.solve(np.eye(k) - gamma * P[np.ix_(idx, idx)], r_hat[idx]). Terminal states keep value 0.
batch_td0 must hold V fixed for a whole sweep. Add each alpha * delta into a separate array, then add that array to V once the sweep ends.
SARSA's target uses the action you will actually take next; Q-learning's uses the max over actions, whatever you take.
Break ties with rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(q_row == q_row.max())). With Q = 0 everywhere, argmax always goes up into the wall.
